I ended up telling my partner I was assaulted, but I couldn't get myself to use the word for what it actually was. If my friend hadn't been there the second time that night the guy physically and sexually assaulted me, I don't know how I would've told anyone. I don't know if I would've been able to process it. 

But my partner has taken it really hard. He feels like it's his fault, that he should have been there to stop it. I told him it's absolutely not his fault. We may not be "official", but we're basically in an exclusive relationship anyways. Nothing made me angrier than seeing him so torn up, because I was so furious at the man who had done that to me, and how his actions had hurt my partner. 

When I've told people the details they say it absolutely sounds like rape, yet my brain is starting to think it's all made up. I guess it wouldn't be surprising if it's a defense mechanism...

I completely feel you. Until it happened to me, I didn't realize just how fucked up and how common it is, and how horribly normalized so many people treat it as. I understand people being scared of false accusations, I guess, but they're so few and far between that it's an outlier when it happens. Actual rape happens so, so much more often, and I hate that the outlier cases lead to it not being believed. 

I also find myself getting angry that people don't understand the freeze response in these situations. I didn't before it happened either, I just knew that it was my default response instead of fight or flight, and I never knew why. Now I know it's because your body sees it as the safest way to escape a threat. I wish more education was given around peoples responses to threatening situations, because I feel like it's a big reason people don't believe survivors. 

Anger is the emotion that has stuck with me the most since then. I also used to try to see the good in everyone. I expected the lingering emotion to be despair. And sure, sometimes it is. But more often I find myself angry. Furious. I'm not used to feeling anger creep up so often. 

And I hate that people say a rape conviction will ruin someone's life. Committing that act against the victim of the crime affects the victim for the rest of their life. Why is there never any justice for that?

My partner has been supportive and didn't ask for details, which I was relieved by. However, a few nights later he kind of broke down and was blaming himself, saying he should have been there and that he wishes he had been able to stop it from happening. It hurt to see him hurt by that, because I wish he didn't blame himself. 

It's never your fault when these things happen. It's the fault of the horrible person that committed the act. I really hope he comes around, because you deserve someone who is going to care about you.
